Notes for my students

Lessons

Each lesson covers one topic, or a narrow set of related topics, and points to the government or manufacturer source behind it. New student pilots start with the items marked ☆; after your first few lessons we will talk about when to add the rest to your reading.

The Library holds the checklists, reading lists and references that cover whole areas of knowledge. Lessons are narrower: one thing, explained.

☆ Start here · Draft VFR airspace at a glance

Entry requirements, equipment and VFR weather minimums for every class of airspace, with Bay Area examples.

 ☆ Start here · Draft The go-around, done right

Deciding early, then power, pitch, flaps and trim in the right order — and the mistakes that turn a normal maneuver into a scary one.

a photo tour of real problems found on the walk-around

Planned Cessna 182 G1000 start procedure

a one-page guide to priming and starting

Planned Flying the pattern

how I fly the traffic pattern at TBDbase airport

Planned Radio primer

Planned Operating at a non-towered airport

Planned Oxygen and altitude

when you need it and how to use it

Lessons marked Draft were written from FAA sources and are being reviewed before they are final. If you spot an error, tell me — that is how they get better.
